problem: WRONG TARGET. The spec maps "Your spells... that deal fire damage gain a status bonus to damage equal to half the spell's rank" to targetKind 'spell'. In this app 'spell' is not a generic spellcasting bucket — src/rules/explain.ts defines it as `{ kind: 'spell'; entryId: string; which: 'dc' | 'attack' }`, i.e. the Spell DC and spell-attack-modifier tiles. Burn It grants NO bonus to spell attack rolls or spell DCs; it boosts the damage the spell deals. Starring the Spell DC / spell attack stat with a damage bonus is exactly the mis-target the brief warns about, and a player reading it would think their attack roll or DC went up.
correction: Keep situational:true and needsEngineWork:true but return ZERO bonuses. All three clauses are damage OUTPUT, which has no target kind: (a) spell fire damage (+half the spell's rank, min +1), (b) alchemical-item fire damage (+one-quarter the item's level, min +1), (c) +1 status to persistent fire damage. engineNote should say the missing capability is a spell-/item-damage-output target, not that one clause maps to 'spell'.

problem: MISSING needsEngineWork FLAG. The engineNote correctly observes that "The attack-roll form of Aid is not covered by a 'skill' target", but the spec leaves needsEngineWork unset. Verified against the Aid reaction (.import-src/pf2e/packs/pf2e/actions/basic/aid.json): "attempt a skill check or attack roll of a type decided by the GM... or even allow you to Aid checks other than skill checks and attack rolls." So skill:'all' provably cannot cover the whole +4. The identical gap (Escape via unarmed attack modifier) WAS flagged needsEngineWork:true on musetouched, so this is an inconsistent flag, not a judgement difference.
correction: Set needsEngineWork:true, keeping the single skill:'all' bonus. engineNote: the attack-roll form of Aid (and any GM-permitted non-skill Aid check) has no representable target — 'strikeAttack' would wrongly star every attack roll.

problem: The classification (situational false) is right, but the stated reason is factually wrong. The record says "You gain the item bonus to attack rolls with your energy blasts from the highest potency rune on any Handwraps of Mighty Blows you are wearing OR ANY WEAPON YOU ARE WIELDING" — that is not "the normal rule" for unarmed attacks (normally only handwraps grant potency to unarmed Strikes; HH's own handwraps buff is guarded on category==='unarmed'). It is a special, non-standard potency source that the engine will not apply on its own.
correction: Keep situational:false and keep needsEngineWork:true, but restate reasonIfNot: "Not a conditional bonus to a character stat — it defines a temporary Strike. Note the potency source is non-standard: the energy blast borrows the highest potency rune from handwraps OR any weapon wielded, so the Strike definition must carry that rule explicitly rather than relying on HH's normal unarmed/handwraps path (striking and property runes do not apply)."

problem: Wrong target. The +1 circumstance bonus is to a kineticist IMPULSE attack roll, and the spec files it under targetKind 'spell' (the spell attack/DC statistic). A kineticist is not a spellcaster and has no spell attack statistic on the sheet, so the star would either never render or — worse, on a dual-class or archetype caster — mark a spell attack the feat never touches. AoN's Kineticist class entry (aon-2e-archive by-category/class/class-23.json) settles it: "Your impulse attack roll uses the same proficiency and attribute modifier as your kineticist class DC... Like a spell attack modifier, your impulse attack modifier uses the following formula" — it is only *like* a spell attack, it IS the class-DC statistic (Con + class DC proficiency, the same track derive.ts uses for Elemental Blast).
correction: Keep situational: true and the condition text ('on the Magnetic Pinions impulse attack roll against a target wearing metal armor or made of metal'). Change targetKind from 'spell' to 'classDc' — the closest legal kind and the statistic the roll is actually built from — and set needsEngineWork: true with the note that an impulse ATTACK ROLL is not the class DC itself (it is that statistic minus 10) and there is no impulse-attack target kind; the same gap affects every kineticist impulse-attack feat. The needsHumanDecision question should be restated as 'should impulse attack rolls get their own target kind, or ride classDc?' rather than 'is spell the right bucket?', which is answered: no.

problem: WRONG TARGET on the second entry. The text is "you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to your Reflex DC to avoid being Disarmed and Tripped" — that is the DC an opponent's Athletics check is rolled against, not a Reflex save the character rolls. Filing it under targetKind 'save'/reflex puts a star on the Reflex save row where a player will read it as "+2 to my Reflex saves under these conditions", which is not what the feat does. The brief explicitly forbids inventing a kind and requires needsEngineWork when the app has no stat for the thing being buffed; the engineer noted the mismatch in engineNote but did not set the flag.
correction: Set needsEngineWork: true with engineNote 'no DC-side channel — a bonus to the character\'s Reflex DC (what Disarm/Trip is rolled against) cannot be expressed by any listed target kind'. Either drop the save/reflex entry until that channel exists, or keep it only if the display renders it as a DC line rather than a save-modifier star. The first entry (+1 circumstance, Athletics to Disarm/Swim/Trip, while in the stance and unarmored) is correct and verified.

problem: WRONG TARGET / sign inversion. The text is "the targets focus on you and gain a +1 circumstance bonus to hit you" — the circumstance bonus sits on the ENEMIES' attack rolls, not on this character's AC. The spec records it as an AC entry with the value '-1 circumstance (effective; enemies get +1 to hit you)' and no needsEngineWork. (I checked the cited precedent and it does exist — situationalBonuses.ts has "barbarian-dedication": [{ targets: [{ kind: 'ac' }], when: "while raging", bonus: "-1 (penalty)" }] — but that one is a real penalty to the character's own AC from Rage, so it is not the same object: here the modifier lives on the attacker's side and competes with the attacker's other circumstance bonuses, not with the character's.)
correction: Keep situational: true but add needsEngineWork: true — 'the modifier is a circumstance bonus on enemy attack rolls against you; no enemy-side / attack-against-you channel exists.' If it is nevertheless shown on AC as an approximation, the entry must render unambiguously as a detriment and must not label the character as holding a -1 circumstance modifier. Also tighten the condition: the effect only lands on enemies that FAIL the check ("On a success" of your check against their Will DCs), lasts 1 round, or 3 rounds on a critical success, and the frequency is once per hour.

problem: The bonus is filed as two self-stars on the owner's Diplomacy and Performance, but the text gives it to someone else: "You spend 1 minute making quick adjustments to SOMEONE'S clothing and appearance ... the TARGET gains a +1 item bonus to Diplomacy and Performance checks." This is the same shape as helpful-halfling, tupilaq-carver, clan-protector and mask-familiar, which the same spec set correctly marked situational:false. As submitted it would put a +1/+2/+3 item star on the Diplomacy and Performance of a character who, in the normal case, gave the bonus away.
correction: Set situational:false with reasonIfNot 'the item bonus is granted to a target creature, not to the feat's owner', keep needsEngineWork:true (no channel for putting a bonus on another PC's sheet) and keep the human question about whether self-targeting should be allowed. If the owner is later ruled a legal target, re-add the two entries but the when must say 'if you spent 1 minute preparing YOUR OWN appearance, while speaking to the chosen audience', and note the size keys off the OWNER's Crafting proficiency (that part of the note is right).

problem: needsEngineWork is missing and the target is the wrong surface. The bonus is to SPELL DAMAGE ("you gain a status bonus to that spell's damage equal to the spell's level"), but targetKind 'spell' is the spell attack/DC surface — there is no spell-damage stat in the allowed kind list (strikeDamage is Strikes only). As submitted, the star lands on spell attack rolls / spell DC, which the feat does not affect at all. That is exactly the 'wrong target' failure mode.
correction: Keep targetKind 'spell' only as the least-bad host, but set needsEngineWork:true with the note 'no spell-damage surface exists; the app has strikeDamage for Strikes and spell for attack/DC, neither of which is spell damage'. The when text must lead with 'to the spell's DAMAGE' so a player reading the spell attack/DC star is not misled. The three-condition wording (from a slot, deals damage, no duration) is correct and the status type is correct.

problem: Self-contradictory record: situational is true but bonuses is an empty array and there is no reasonIfNot. The record's own text confirms the only typed bonus goes to the ENEMY ("The target of your Strike gains a +4 circumstance bonus to their Perception DC for this check"); the character gets nothing conditional. A consumer that branches on situational===true will look for entries and find none, and the chunk's own convention for 'no player-facing bonus' (lavasoul, spell-swipe) is situational:false + reasonIfNot.
correction: Set situational:false with reasonIfNot: "No bonus to any of the character's stats. The feat's only typed bonus (+4 circumstance) is granted to the Strike's target, raising their Perception DC and making the character's own Stealth check HARDER. It must never be recorded as a bonus for the character." Keep needsEngineWork:true only if the project wants to track enemy-side modifiers; otherwise drop it.

problem: The condition is broader than the rules allow. The bonus rides on Arcane Cascade, and the Arcane Cascade action in core.json says "While you're in the stance, your melee Strikes deal 1 extra force damage" — melee only. The spec's `when` never says melee, so a starlit span magus (whose ranged Spellstrikes get no Arcane Cascade damage at all) would see a strike-damage star that never applies to the attacks they actually make. The spec also implies Arcane Cascade's own damage is a bonus; it is a flat extra-damage rider of 1/2/3 (force, or the triggering spell's type).
correction: Rewrite the `when` as: "on MELEE Strikes only, until the end of your next turn, after you resist a foe's harmful spell while already in Arcane Cascade — the +2 status raises the Arcane Cascade extra damage (1/2/3 by weapon specialization), not the whole damage roll." Keep targetKind strikeDamage, needsEngineWork:true.

problem: The classification (unconditional, belongs in the maths) is right, but needsEngineWork:false is wrong. NO feat record in core.json carries a `saves` field — I counted 0 across the whole feats collection — so there is no data lane by which an unconditional feat-granted save bonus can reach the computed total. Marking it situational:false with no engine flag means the +2 status bonus to Fortitude and Will vanishes from the sheet entirely: not in the number, not on a star.
correction: Keep situational:false, but set needsEngineWork:true: "core.json has no feat-level `saves` field (0 feats carry one) and derive.ts has no feat→save lane, so this unconditional +2 status to Fortitude and Will is currently invisible. A `saves` grant field on feats (parallel to the existing `speeds` field, 72 feats) is needed before 'it belongs in the maths' is true."

problem: Structurally broken: situational is true but the spec carries NO bonuses array at all (only needsEngineWork + engineNote). A record flagged situational with zero entries either fails the loader or stars a stat with nothing to display. The engineNote's own reasoning ('no allowed target kind fits, using strikeDamage would put the marker on the wrong statistic') is the argument for NOT marking this character at all.
correction: Flip to situational:false with reasonIfNot: 'The bonus applies to the damage of the Destructive Vengeance champion reaction, which is neither a Strike nor a spell — no allowed target kind can hold it, and strikeDamage would mark the wrong statistic. Nothing on this character's own sheet changes.' Keep needsEngineWork:true and the engineNote (variable size = the reaction's damage dice count; applies only to the enemy's share, not the self-damage). Text verified: 'You gain a circumstance bonus to the damage you deal from Destructive Vengeance equal to the number of damage dice from the reaction.'

problem: needsEngineWork:false contradicts its own engineNote ('when the ally is the target the bonus belongs on their sheet, which the app cannot show') and is inconsistent with how the same self-or-ally structure was flagged elsewhere in this batch — known-weaknesses, connect-the-dots, clue-them-all-in and lead-investigator all set needsEngineWork:true for exactly the missing 'bonus conferred on another character' lane. A downstream pass filtering on needsEngineWork will not see this gap.
correction: Set needsEngineWork:true, engineNote: 'Missing target — a bonus conferred on an ally's AC. Only the self case (you are the target of the triggering ranged attack) is representable.' The bonus itself is verified correct: '+2 circumstance bonus to AC against the triggering attack', targetKind ac, situational true.

problem: Same defect as snap-falling-fruit: needsEngineWork:false while the engineNote states the ally case is 'not representable'. Inconsistent with the true flag used for every other ally-conferred bonus in this batch.
correction: Set needsEngineWork:true, engineNote: 'Missing target — a bonus conferred on an ally's AC (trigger reaches an ally within 10 feet). Only the self case is representable.' The bonus is verified correct against 'You or the triggering ally gain a +2 circumstance bonus to AC against the triggering attack.'

problem: The lore skill key is wrong. The spec uses target skill `lore:bardic-lore`. The app's canonical lore key is `lore:<subject>` with the word "Lore" STRIPPED — `loreKey()` in src/builder/shared.tsx:3061-3068 does `.replace(/\blore\b/g, '')`, so "Bardic Lore" canonicalises to `lore:bardic`. Worse, `loreLabel()` (shared.tsx:3051-3057) appends " Lore" to the slug, so `lore:bardic-lore` would render as "Bardic Lore Lore" and would never match the character's actual proficiency key. The spec also files this under needsHumanDecision:false / needsEngineWork:true with the key marked "assumed" — the key is answerable from the code, no assumption needed.
correction: Use skill `lore:bardic`. Keep needsEngineWork:true, but only for the real gap: the entry must be gated on the character also having the `bardic-lore` feat (core.json feats['bardic-lore'] exists), and the registry has no second-feat predicate. Entry: { targets: [{ kind: 'skill', detail: 'lore:bardic' }], when: "on Bardic Lore checks (only if you have the Bardic Lore class feat)", bonus: "+1 circumstance" }.

problem: The condition is broadened — it drops the tradition restriction from the BONUS and states it only on the trigger. Spellmaster's Resilience (core.json, verified) gives "+1 circumstance bonus to saving throws against spells and effects with that tradition's trait"; Tenacity only says "increase the circumstance bonus to saving throws from the Spellmaster's Resilience feat to +2". The spec's `when` reads "for 1 minute after this reaction fires — once per day, when you critically fail a save against a foe's spell of your chosen tradition", which a player will read as +2 to ALL saves for 1 minute. Second problem: spellmasters-resilience is ALREADY in the registry (situationalBonuses.ts line 309, targets save/all, when "against spells and effects of your chosen tradition", bonus "+1 circumstance"), so adding this as a plain "+2 circumstance" entry puts two save stars on the sheet that read as stacking (+1 and +2) rather than one replacing the other.
correction: Re-word the `when` to carry the tradition restriction on the bonus itself and mark it as a replacement: { targets: [{ kind: 'save', detail: 'all' }], when: "against spells and effects of your chosen tradition, for 1 minute after this reaction (once per day, when you critically fail such a save)", bonus: "+2 circumstance (replaces Spellmaster's Resilience's +1; its resistance also rises to 10)" }. Flag needsEngineWork:true for the real gap — the registry cannot express "this entry supersedes entry X while active", so both stars will show at once.

problem: The engineNote's list of panache-granting skills is factually wrong. It says "Acrobatics / Athletics / Deception / Diplomacy / Intimidation". Verified against core.json classFeatures: battledancer = Performance, braggart = Intimidation, fencer = Deception, gymnast = Athletics, rascal = Thievery (Dirty Trick), wit = Diplomacy (Bon Mot). So Performance and Thievery are missing, and Acrobatics is not a style skill at all — Acrobatics comes from Tumble Through, which the `panache` class feature grants the bravado trait for EVERY swashbuckler, and which the spec already covers in its own separate entry. Anyone using that note to narrow the target later would silently drop two styles.
correction: Fix the note to: styles are Performance (battledancer), Intimidation (braggart), Deception (fencer), Athletics (gymnast), Thievery (rascal), Diplomacy (wit); Acrobatics is the universal Tumble Through clause, not a style. Also set needsEngineWork:true — the app DOES know the chosen style (classFeatures battledancer/braggart/fencer/gymnast/rascal/wit), so narrowing skill 'all' to the one style skill is a real, doable engine improvement rather than a hypothetical. The three bonuses' sizes, types and the qualifying-condition list (clumsy, drained, enfeebled, frightened, sickened, stupefied) are confirmed correct.

problem: The save is broadened to 'all'. The record says the bonus applies "on their ongoing saves against poisons already present in their body". Poison is an affliction, and PF2e affliction/poison ongoing saves are Fortitude saves; there is no poison that calls for an ongoing Reflex or Will save. Starring Reflex and Will with "against poisons" tells a player at the table to add +2 to rolls that will never happen. The spec's stated reason ("to avoid over-narrowing") is also the opposite of the call it made on glyph-expert, where an unnamed skill was narrowed to one.
correction: Use save 'fortitude': { targets: [{ kind: 'save', detail: 'fortitude' }], when: "for 1 minute, on ongoing saves against poisons already in the body when you cast cleanse cuisine on the creature (you or a touched ally)", bonus: "+2 status" }. Keep needsEngineWork:true for the correct reason the spec gave — the spell can be cast on a touched ally, so the bonus may land on someone else.

problem: Wrong target: narrowed to save/fortitude on a bonus the text never restricts to a save type. The record reads "granting a +1 item bonus to saves and DCs against attempts to grapple or swallow you" — "saves" is unqualified, so any save prompted by a grapple/swallow attempt (e.g. a Reflex save against an effect that grabs you) qualifies. Foundry's own rule element for this item confirms it: selector ["saving-throw","fortitude-dc","reflex-dc","will-dc"], i.e. ALL saves plus all three DCs, predicated on action:grapple / action:swallow-whole. The spec's engineNote also contradicts its own choice: it states the practically important half is the Fortitude DC (which the player never rolls), then anchors the marker on the Fortitude save row — so the one row that gets a star is the roll least likely to happen, and Reflex/Will get no marker at all.
correction: Keep situational:true, +1 item, but set targetKind save with save:'all' (the registry's existing convention, as used by affliction-resistance / adaptive-vision). when: "against attempts to Grapple or Swallow you (the same bonus also applies to your Fortitude, Reflex and Will DCs against those attempts)". Leave needsEngineWork:true for the DC half (no save-DC target kind exists) and the needsHumanDecision question as written.

id: alcohol, bloodeye-coffee, flayleaf, blood-sap, elven-absinthe, scour, sun-orchid-poultice, vaccine, bloodhound-mask (+ -lesser/-moderate/-greater), addiction-suppressant (+ -lesser/-moderate/-greater/-major)

Since the registry keys off records the character has, an engine-work triage that filters on needsEngineWork will ship all of these as possession-triggered stars: carrying a flask of alcohol would permanently star your saves, and carrying an unused bloodhound mask would star Survival. The bonus values, types and targets in this group are all verified correct against the records.
correction: Set needsEngineWork:true on every consumable/drug record in the chunk, with the note "requires an active-effect gate (drug stage or elixir duration), not inventory possession". Uniformly, so the flag can be used as the triage filter.

problem: Encoding bug: situational is true but there is NO bonuses array, so the entry is empty. The reading itself is right ('If the animal companion already has scent, IT gains a +2 circumstance bonus to Perception when using scent against fiends' — the companion, not the PC), but every other other-creature case in this same batch is encoded situational:false + needsEngineWork:true (guiding-shot, shielded-recovery, area-armor, shield-from-arrows, blanket-defense, lesson-of-the-broken-wing). As written this record is inconsistent and would either produce a registry entry with nothing to display or, worse, a star on the PC with no text.
correction: Set situational:false with reasonIfNot 'The +2 circumstance bonus is to the animal companion's Perception, not the character's', and keep needsEngineWork:true + engineNote 'needs a companion-stat situational lane; conditions are doubly narrow (only when the companion uses its scent sense, and only against fiends)'.

problem: CLASSIFICATION IS RIGHT, needsEngineWork IS WRONG. The record text is confirmed unconditional ("In addition, you gain a +2 status bonus to Fortitude and Will saving throws." — no trigger, requirement or duration), so situational:false is correct. But the spec asserts it "belongs in the computed save totals" without checking whether it is there. It is not: the core.json record has keys id,name,level,category,traits,rarity,description,source,prerequisites,actionCost,edition and NO `saves` field; a scan shows ZERO feats in core.json carry a `saves` field at all; and grepping C:\trying ai 2\pf2e codex\src for 'peerless-form' returns no matches. The +2 status to Fortitude and Will is currently applied nowhere in the app. Excluding it from this registry as written leaves it silently missing — the exact mirror of the monk-moves defect the same engineer correctly caught.
correction: Keep situational:false, but set needsEngineWork:true with the note: "No feat record in core.json carries a `saves` field and nothing in src references peerless-form, so this unconditional +2 status to Fortitude and Will is not applied by the engine. Either add a feat-level `saves` lane (mirroring the existing `speeds` lane) and backfill peerless-form, or the bonus is lost entirely."

problem: The classification (situational:false, bonus lands on an ALLY's AC) is CORRECT and confirmed by the text. The engineNote's factual claims about the duplicates are WRONG on both counts. It says 'guardians-deflection' is "raw AoN-style text, no level field" — that record DOES have level 4 and category 'class'. It says 'guardians-deflection-swashbuckler' is the "level 4, tidied text" one — true, but that record is marked edition:"superseded", i.e. it is the one already suppressed, not the survivor. The note also misses a THIRD record entirely: 'guardians-deflection-fighter' (Fighter, level 6, edition remaster), a distinct live feat with the same ally-AC-only behaviour.
correction: Keep situational:false and needsEngineWork:true (no target kind for another creature's AC). Replace the note with: "Three records exist: 'guardians-deflection' (swashbuckler, level 4, remaster, raw-text formatting) and 'guardians-deflection-fighter' (fighter, level 6, remaster) are both LIVE and both grant the +2 circumstance only to the ally's AC; 'guardians-deflection-swashbuckler' (level 4) is already edition:'superseded'. Any decision must cover the two live ids."

problem: The classification (situational:false, the +1 circumstance is on the ALLY's Will save) is CORRECT and confirmed. The engineNote's duplicate claim is WRONG in the same way as guardians-deflection: 'snap-out-of-it' DOES have a level field (4), and the "tidied" record is 'snap-out-of-it-marshal', which is already edition:"superseded". More importantly, the note's instruction that "a decision here should cover both" is dangerous because there is a THIRD id, 'snap-out-of-it-pathfinder-agent' (level 8, Pathfinder Agent archetype), which is a DIFFERENT feat — a Medicine check that reduces the value of fascinated/frightened/stunned/stupefied. It grants no typed bonus at all and must not inherit this classification.
correction: Keep situational:false and needsEngineWork:true. Replace the note with: "'snap-out-of-it' (level 4, remaster) is the live record; 'snap-out-of-it-marshal' is already edition:'superseded'. 'snap-out-of-it-pathfinder-agent' is an unrelated feat (Medicine check that reduces a condition's value) with no typed bonus — exclude it, do not apply this decision to it."

problem: The spec records an entry on this character's own AC with bonus "-1 circumstance (effective; enemies get +1 to hit you)". The record grants this character no bonus and no penalty. Verified text: "On a success, the targets focus on you and gain a +1 circumstance bonus to hit you, but they're off-guard to all creatures other than yourself." That is a bonus on the ENEMIES' attack rolls — the same category the very same pass correctly flagged needsEngineWork for exigent-aura ("the +4 is a bonus on the ENEMY's saving throw"). Converting it to an AC penalty is also mechanically wrong, not just cosmetically: a circumstance bonus in the attacker's pool competes with THEIR circumstance modifiers (flanking, etc.), whereas a circumstance penalty on your AC competes with YOURS (cover, Raise a Shield). The two produce different numbers whenever either side already has a circumstance modifier. The engineNote's cited precedent is not analogous either — barbarian Rage is written as a penalty to the raging character's own AC; Primadonna is not.
correction: situational: true, needsEngineWork: true, bonuses: [] (remove the ac entry). engineNote: "Enemies within 30 feet who see or hear you and fail against your Performance check gain a +1 circumstance bonus to attack rolls against you for 1 round (3 rounds on a critical success); they are off-guard to everyone else. The only numeric modifier is on the ENEMY's attack roll, so there is nothing to mark on this character's own stats — needs an enemy-side modifier channel, same as exigent-aura. Do not re-express it as a -1 circumstance penalty to AC: that lands in the wrong stacking pool."

problem: The second bonus entry maps "+2 circumstance bonus to your Reflex DC to avoid being Disarmed and Tripped" (verified verbatim) onto targetKind 'save', save 'reflex', and needsEngineWork is NOT set. A Reflex DC is the number an opponent rolls against; it is not a Reflex saving throw this character rolls. As written the entry paints a star on the player's Reflex SAVE row for a bonus that never applies to any save they make. The spec's own engineNote concedes "A DC-side channel would be more correct" but the flag that records exactly that gap was left off, so the wrong entry would ship. (The first entry, +1 circumstance to Athletics to Disarm/Swim/Trip, is verified correct and should stay.)
correction: Keep only the athletics entry: {bonus: '+1 circumstance', when: 'while in Reflective Ripple Stance (unarmored), on Athletics checks to Disarm, Swim, or Trip', targetKind: 'skill', skill: 'athletics'}. Drop the save/reflex entry and set needsEngineWork: true with engineNote: "The stance also gives +2 circumstance to your Reflex DC against attempts to Disarm or Trip you. That is a defence DC others roll against, and no target kind in the list represents a DC — it must not be recorded on save/reflex. Needs a defence-DC channel."

problem: The single perception entry merges two different things into one 'when' string: (a) "Perception checks made to Sense Motive against other elves" and (b) "your Perception DC against Lies spoken by agents of Tanglebriar". I confirmed Political Acumen's text in core.json reads exactly that way, so the inherited condition is right — but (b) is a DC opponents roll against, not a Perception check this character rolls, and needsEngineWork is not set. Same defect as reflective-ripple-stance: half the entry is a stat the app has no representation for, silently folded into a target kind that does exist.
correction: Split into one representable entry plus a flag. Entry: {bonus: '+4 circumstance (replaces Political Acumen's +2)', when: 'on Perception checks to Sense Motive against other elves', targetKind: 'perception'}. Then needsEngineWork: true, engineNote: "Political Acumen's other half — +2 (raised to +4 by this feat) to your Perception DC against Lies spoken by agents of Tanglebriar — is a DC others roll against and has no target kind; needs a defence-DC channel. Also, when both feats are held Political Acumen's +2 must be suppressed rather than stacked."

problem: The classification (needsEngineWork for a counteract check) is correct and verified, but the engineNote asserts a fact not present in the record: "the counteract modifier here is your Occultism/Religion-style modifier chosen at use time". The record's actual text has the skill names missing entirely — it reads "you use either your or modifier as your counteract modifier" (two literal blanks where the importer dropped the skill links). Naming Occultism/Religion is a guess layered on top of a data defect rather than something grounded in the record.
correction: Keep situational: true and needsEngineWork: true. Rewrite the engineNote to: "The +1 circumstance bonus applies to a COUNTERACT CHECK, which is not one of the available target kinds — needs a counteract-check channel. Note the record's description is also damaged: it reads 'you use either your or modifier as your counteract modifier', with the two skill names stripped by the importer, so the counteract modifier cannot be resolved from this data at all." Worth surfacing separately as a core.json text defect.

problem: needsEngineWork is set to false, but the spec targets 'strikeDamage', which is not a member of SituationalTarget.kind in src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts ('skill' | 'save' | 'perception' | 'ac' | 'attack'). The entry cannot be stored or displayed as specified. The text and bonus reading itself is correct: "You gain a circumstance bonus to damage for the Strike equal to twice the number of weapon damage dice."
correction: Set needsEngineWork: true — the registry needs a strikeDamage (or generic damage) target kind before this can be shown; the variable size (2x weapon damage dice) is a second, separate engine need already noted.

problem: Two issues. (1) needsEngineWork:false is wrong for the same reason as pivot-strike — 'strikeDamage' is not a supported target kind. (crown-of-intellect legitimately uses 'all' — its text literally says "regardless of the skill" — so the two records must not be encoded the same way.)
correction: Replace the single skill:'all' entry with the seven named skills plus Lore. The registry's SituationalBonus shape is targets: SituationalTarget[], so this is one bonus with seven-plus targets: [{kind:'skill',detail:'arcana'},{...'crafting'},{...'medicine'},{...'nature'},{...'occultism'},{...'religion'},{...'society'}] (plus the character's lore:* keys), when: "to Recall Knowledge with the one skill you chose when you Skimmed the tome, after spending an Interact action to peruse it (the pages last 24 hours)", bonus: "+3 item". Keep needsEngineWork:true only for the narrower ask — a per-activation chosen-skill selector so the star lands on the single chosen skill rather than all eight candidates.

problem: The classification (situational:false for the wearer; the conditional bonus goes to an ally) is correct, but the engineNote states a false reason: "(b) the bonus size is variable (equal to the wearer's cursebound condition value), which the fixed 'bonus' string cannot express." The registry's bonus field is a free string and already carries variable magnitudes — deathless-servant: "status bonus equal to your wounded value"; disarming-intercept: "item bonus equal to your armor's potency rune"; mutant-physique: "mutagen's item bonus"; necromantic-deflection: "shield's circumstance bonus". Leaving this in would send the app owner to build engine work that already exists.
correction: Keep situational:false and needsEngineWork:true, but reduce the engineNote to the one real gap: the bonus targets ANOTHER character's saving throw and there is no target kind for an ally's stat (the closest precedent, terrain-scout, records an ally effect as bonus: "ally benefit (no roll bonus)" on the wearer's own stat). Delete the variable-magnitude claim — "status bonus equal to your cursebound value" is already an expressible bonus string.

problem: Same false engineNote as the base veil: "a variable magnitude tied to the wearer's cursebound value" is presented as an engine gap. Variable-magnitude bonus strings are already supported and in use in src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts.
correction: Keep situational:false and needsEngineWork:true; the only genuine gap is the ally-targeted save/attack roll (no target kind for another character's stat). Remove the variable-magnitude half of the note.

problem: The spec sets situational:true but supplies no `bonuses` array at all, so the record classifies as situational while producing zero registry rows. A consumer keying off `situational` gets an entry it cannot author; a consumer keying off `bonuses` drops it entirely. The record's text is confirmed ("If you are a demon, it amplifies any auras you have by granting a +1 item bonus to your aura's DCs.") and the reasoning — no aura-DC target exists, classDc would be the wrong stat, and the app has no creature-type gate for the PC — is correct.
correction: Set situational:false with needsEngineWork:true and put the analysis in reasonIfNot/engineNote: "+1 item bonus to your auras' DCs, only if you are a demon — no representable target (aura DC is not classDc, and the app has no PC creature-type gate)." That keeps the record out of the registry without a true-but-empty row.

problem: The DATA call (situational:false) is right, but the engineNote makes a false factual claim about the app: "this weapon's attack modifier is currently 2 too low when thrown". Alchemical bombs are not weapons in core.json at all — `d.items['greater-defoliation-bomb']` (and every one of the 254 bomb-trait items, e.g. moderate-nail-bomb, alchemist's-fire, bottled-lightning) is `itemType: "equipment"` with no `category`, `group`, `damage` or `hands` field, unlike `longsword` which has `itemType: "weapon", category: "martial", group: "sword", damage: {dice:1,die:"d8",type:"slashing"}`. There is no Strike for the app to be "2 too low" on. The same understated note is repeated on the other 15 graded-bomb specs (major-defoliation-bomb, moderate/greater/major nail-bomb, moderate/greater/major inflammation-flask, moderate/greater/major spider-satchel, moderate/greater/major durian-bomb, moderate/greater/major tenderizer-grenade), all phrased as if a bomb Strike existed and only the item bonus were missing.
correction: Keep situational:false and needsEngineWork:true, but restate the note: bombs are not modeled as weapons (itemType 'equipment', no damage/category/group), so they produce no Strike at all; the engine work needed is bomb-as-thrown-weapon support (damage dice, splash, bomb proficiency) with the grade's item bonus to attack rolls fed into that Strike's item slot — derive.ts's `potencyBonus` (line 1188: `Math.max(abpOn(c) ? abpAttack(c.level) : runes?.potency ?? 0, mpRef?.attack ?? 0)`) reads runes/ABP/Monster-Parts only and would need a third source. Verified correct in these specs: the quoted grade texts, the +1/+2/+3 progression, and that the lesser grade of every family grants no attack bonus.

problem: The engineNote asserts "The base +3 item bonus from the major resilient rune is UNCONDITIONAL and belongs in the armour maths; only the extra +1 against poison is situational, so the star should read as 'a +4 instead of +3'". That claim is false for this record. The core.json entry for slithermaws-bane-artifact has NO usage field, no armor category, no runes and no save entries in passiveEffects (its passiveEffects contains only the poison resistance 15). The +3 major resilient bonus is therefore nowhere in the app's maths, so a star that reads "+4 instead of +3" points the player at a baseline number the sheet never shows. The bonus values themselves (+4 item vs poison, +2 circumstance after Adaptation) are correct and are correctly typed.
correction: Keep both bonus entries as specified, but fix the framing: the first entry should read as a plain "+4 item bonus to saving throws against poison" with an explanatory clause ("the major resilient rune's +3, raised by 1 against poison") rather than "+4 instead of +3", and the record should carry needsEngineWork: true noting that this artifact is not modelled as armour at all (no usage/armor/rune data), so the underlying resilient +3 is missing from every save total. Also, the second entry's duration is slightly under-stated: the text says the Adaptation effect lasts "until your next daily preparations or the next time you activate it, whichever comes first" — add the second clause.

problem: The spec says only the Stealth penalty belongs in the maths and treats the sight-only Perception bonus as a clean situational entry with needsEngineWork:false. So the app currently applies a sight-ONLY bonus to every Perception check (hearing, scent, Seek by smell), and adding a star on top would double-report the same +1.

The passiveEffects.skills.stealth = -1 is correct and must stay.

problem: Marked situational:false. The record says "Your clockwork components allow you to react to danger with alacrity. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to initiative rolls." The spec's own reasoning ('unconditional within its scope') conflates 'no extra trigger' with 'unconditional relative to the stat it is filed under'. Filed as targetKind perception, situational:false reads as 'fold this into the maths' — which would add +2 to Perception permanently and inflate Seek, Sense Motive and the passive Perception DC, exactly the failure mode the brief warns about. The spec's own engineNote even says 'It must NOT be added to the Perception total', contradicting the flag.
correction: Set situational: true. Keep the single entry {targetKind:'perception', bonus:'+2 circumstance', when:'on initiative rolls (Perception, or whichever skill you roll initiative with)'} and keep needsEngineWork:true for the missing initiative stat. This matches the two established precedents already in src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts line 49 ("all-this-has-happened-before": perception, 'on your initiative roll (once per day)') and line 52 ("ambush-awareness": perception, 'on Perception checks rolled for initiative'), both of which are situational entries.

problem: Mis-targeted. The record says "a +2 status bonus to your Fortitude DC and Reflex DC against any effect that would move you or knock you prone" — that is the DC an opponent rolls against (Athletics to Shove/Trip/Grapple), which in PF2e is 10 + your save modifier, NOT your save roll. The spec still emits two entries with targetKind 'save' (fortitude and reflex), so the registry would put a star on the Fortitude and Reflex rows. A player opening those rows reads "+2 status" as a boost to the d20 roll — exactly the 'misleads the player' failure mode. The parenthetical disclaimer is buried inside the `bonus` string, which is rendered as the modifier text, not as a caveat.
correction: Emit NO bonus entries for this record. Keep situational: true only in the sense of 'has a conditional effect', set bonuses: [] with needsEngineWork: true / needsHumanDecision: true and the note that the target is a save DC (Fortitude DC / Reflex DC) for which the sheet has no stat — the target-kind list has 'ac' and 'classDc' but no save DC. If the owner later answers 'surface it on the save row', it must be re-added with the disclaimer in a dedicated field the sheet actually renders (e.g. folded into `when`: "this raises your Fortitude DC that an opponent rolls against — it does NOT add to your Fortitude save roll"), never in `bonus`. Everything else in the spec is confirmed: +2 status, 1-action Stand Firm, Frequency once per minute, effects last 1 round, 10 temporary HP is a play resource, and the ally-in-aura gap is real.

problem: Same defect as the Greater banner. These effects last for 1 round." The +3 is a bonus to the DC opponents roll against, but the spec anchors it to targetKind 'save' (fortitude and reflex), which would display it as a bonus to the player's save rolls.

problem: Marked situational:true while emitting ZERO bonuses. The record's own text — "When you affix these ... to the hooves of an ordinary horse or a quadrupedal animal companion and the animal companion invests them, that creature gains a +5-foot item bonus to its land Speed and a +2 circumstance bonus to Athletics checks" — gives everything to the mount, nothing to the PC. A true flag with an empty bonuses array is internally inconsistent and will read downstream as "this record has situational bonuses" when it stars nothing.

Keep needsEngineWork:true and the existing engineNote about the missing companion-stat target kind, and keep the passiveEffects.speedBonus 5 warning — I confirmed it is a live bug (derive.ts:1584 adds it to the PC's land Speed).
